root_cause.text: The per-IO `UBLK_IO_FLAG_CANCELED` flag was only cleared for all IOs in a queue when every IO in that queue had been fetched, so if the server died after fetching only a subset, those fetched IOs retained the flag and could never be canceled by `ublk_cancel_cmd`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the flag reset from `ublk_queue_reset_io_flags` (which waited until all IOs were ready) into the per-IO `ublk_mark_io_ready` function, called immediately after each individual IO is fetched. The commit message explicitly states: "the per-IO canceled flags for all IOs in a queue are reset together only once all IOs for that queue have been fetched. So if a nonempty proper subset of the IOs for a queue are fetched when the ublk server dies, the IOs in that subset will never successfully be canceled."

The group's changes directly address the flag reset issue for per-IO state, which is central to the vulnerability root cause where the UBLK_IO_FLAG_CANCELED flag was not cleared properly for fetched IOs.

candidates.rationale: This line, inside a loop over all IOs in the queue, clears the cancel flag for all IOs in one batch only when the entire queue is ready. It fails to clear the flag on a per-IO basis when each IO is fetched, so if not all IOs are fetched, fetched IOs retain the flag and cannot be canceled later.

The loop header implements the batch clearing by iterating over all IOs, which is the root cause mechanism: the flag is not cleared individually per IO but only when all IOs in the queue are processed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This assignment clears the UBLK_IO_FLAG_CANCELED flag for all IOs in the queue only when the loop runs after all IOs have been fetched. It fails to clear the flag on a per-IO basis when each IO is fetched, so fetched IOs retain the flag and cannot be canceled later if not all IOs are fetched.

This loop header implements the batch clearing of the cancel flag over all IOs in the queue. The vulnerability arises because the flag is only cleared when the entire queue is processed (i.e., all IOs are fetched), rather than clearing it individually per IO at fetch time.
